findings.code_snippet:
## Configuration

Setup does not authorize enterprise installation/maintenance. Disclose packages/maintenance; preserve opt-outs, edits, owners and choices. Never install optional Standards. For QODO_NOTICE/repeated Kiro read approvals read [host-recovery.md](references/host-recovery.md). CLI owns credentials/transport/updates; lifecycle owners update skills.
## Error Handling

Report the error and one next action. Never claim readiness after failure, disable Keychain, copy credentials, change permissions or offer unrestricted approvals.
findings.message: Skill modifies its own code, configuration, or behavior at runtime. Self-modification enables an agent to escalate privileges, disable safety constraints, or install persistent backdoors.
findings.remediation: Prevent the skill from modifying its own code, SKILL.md, or configuration files. Treat skill files as read-only at runtime.

findings.code_snippet:
## Repeated Kiro read approvals

When the host is Kiro and safe reads prompt repeatedly, explain the optional persistent rule before
the next read. The only broad pattern to offer is `<qodo> read *`: that CLI gateway rejects every
managed tool not explicitly marked non-mutating by the live catalog. Keep the version probe as its
own exact `<qodo> --version` rule. Never suggest `<qodo> *` or `<qodo> codebase *`, and never edit
findings.message: Skill injects content designed to persist in agent memory or context across interactions. Persistent injection can alter agent behavior long after the initial interaction.
findings.remediation: Do not allow untrusted input to persist in agent memory or context. Validate all content before storing and implement memory isolation between sessions.

findings.message: Code accesses credential files (SSH keys, AWS credentials, etc.). This could indicate credential theft attempts.
findings.remediation: Remove references to credential paths. Use environment variables or secrets managers. For docs, use placeholder paths (e.g., /path/to/config). Never load .env or token files in production code paths.

findings.code_snippet:
## Configuration

Setup does not authorize enterprise installation/maintenance. Disclose packages/maintenance; preserve opt-outs, edits, owners and choices. Never install optional Standards. For QODO_NOTICE/repeated Kiro read approvals read [host-recovery.md](references/host-recovery.md). CLI owns credentials/transport/updates; lifecycle owners update skills.
## Error Handling

Report the error and one next action. Never claim readiness after failure, disable Keychain, copy credentials, change permissions or offer unrestricted approvals.
findings.message: Skill modifies its own code, configuration, or behavior at runtime. Self-modification enables an agent to escalate privileges, disable safety constraints, or install persistent backdoors.
findings.remediation: Prevent the skill from modifying its own code, SKILL.md, or configuration files. Treat skill files as read-only at runtime.

findings.code_snippet:
## Repeated Kiro read approvals

When the host is Kiro and safe reads prompt repeatedly, explain the optional persistent rule before
the next read. The only broad pattern to offer is `<qodo> read *`: that CLI gateway rejects every
managed tool not explicitly marked non-mutating by the live catalog. Keep the version probe as its
own exact `<qodo> --version` rule. Never suggest `<qodo> *` or `<qodo> codebase *`, and never edit
findings.message: Skill injects content designed to persist in agent memory or context across interactions. Persistent injection can alter agent behavior long after the initial interaction.
findings.remediation: Do not allow untrusted input to persist in agent memory or context. Validate all content before storing and implement memory isolation between sessions.
